description: Two things get bumped here, and config:recommended finds both without
help: the `FROM` pin in each image's Dockerfile, and the actions each
workflow `uses:`.
Renovate does the merging itself rather than handing the pull request to
GitHub's auto-merge, which needs the repository setting turned on and a
required check configured on the branch to wait for anything -- without
those it merges the moment the pull request opens, before the build has
run. Renovate waits for the branch to be green either way.
A new upstream release should become a published tag without waiting
for someone to click merge, since merging to the default branch is
what publishes and the build has already checked the image does what
it exists to do. Majors are left for a person: a new major of a base
image is a different image, and of an action, a changed contract.
analytics-mcp's requirements.txt is a lock compiled for Python 3.13
(the `--python-version 3.13` in its header), installed into the stock
python image. A new minor of the image alone would install 3.13's lock
on 3.14, so the image stays on 3.13 until someone recompiles the lock
for the next minor in the same pull request. Patch releases of 3.13 come
through, and merge themselves, under the rule above.
The lock itself is the pip-compile manager's: it reads the `uv pip
compile` command out of requirements.txt, bumps requirements.in and
re-locks. Those bumps are not merged automatically -- a new release of
an experimental package that reads analytics is worth a look first.
pip_requirements is off because the pip-compile manager's documentation
asks for it: it would otherwise read the lock too and bump its pins one
at a time, under it.
